info.title: Citizen's Edge Companion WebSocket API
info.description: Generated from crates/ce-protocol/protocol.schema.json and ce_core::scope. The readable guide (connecting, scopes, elevation, HTTP routes) is docs/PROTOCOL.md. Every client message needs the scope in `x-scope`; a request may carry `requestId`, which the reply echoes.

local.description: The daemon binds 127.0.0.1 (--port, --host). A browser page must match the Origin allowlist; a native client sends no Origin.

pairingToken.name: Sec-WebSocket-Protocol
pairingToken.description: The pairing token in the data dir, offered as the subprotocol `ce.token.<token>` (a browser cannot set headers). `Authorization: Bearer <token>` also works, and `?token=` for older pages.

examples.name: Ask for admin on this connection
examples.summary: The Companion answers with `auth.elevation` (a six-digit code); the user then runs `ce-companion approve <code>` on this PC.

examples.name: Say you have a blueprint the log did not report
examples.summary: `name` is the blueprint's name as the game shows it; the Companion matches it case-insensitively. `enabled: false` says you do not have it.

examples.name: Delete a contact
examples.summary: Needs `admin`. Removes the contact's rows and suppresses the name so it is not re-created.

examples.name: How you know someone
examples.summary: `category` is one of `my-org`, `org-affiliate`, `alliance`, `friend`, `frequent-party`, `mission-partner`, `encountered`, `stranger`, or `null` to go back to the Companion's own decision.

examples.name: Hostile contacts seen in chat, first 25
examples.summary: `stance` filters on the decided stance (`kos` and `hostile` both count unless `exact`); `source` is where the player was seen; `requestId` comes back on the reply.

examples.name: Who is near me now
examples.summary: `view`: `here` (nearby in 15 minutes), `shared` (same shard, 2 hours) or `all`. Leave it out for the configured window.

examples.name: Mark a player hostile, with a note

payload.note: Pulled a gun at Port Tressler

examples.summary: A personal tag stays on this PC. `tag` is `kos`, `hostile`, `wary`, `neutral`, `friendly`, `ally` or `null` to clear it. `note` is free text up to 500 characters.

examples.name: An officer's org tag
examples.summary: Needs `admin` (a native client, or a page after `ce-companion approve`) and an officer role on the Hub. `org` is the SID the tag applies to; leave it out for your main org. The tag is shared with the org.

examples.name: Preview the storage cleanup
examples.summary: Needs `admin`. `dryRun: true` changes nothing and returns what would be reduced or expired.

examples.name: Start the live feed after the last event you have
examples.summary: `since` is the `seq` of the last `event` you received (the `cursor` of the snapshot on first connect). Omit it to get only new events.

examples.name: Accept one suggestion
examples.summary: `id` is the suggestion's `id` from `suggestions.list`.

examples.name: Share confirmed sightings and presence, not stock or blueprints
examples.summary: Needs `admin`. `sightings` is `off`, `confirmed` or `auto`; the others are on/off. Fields you leave out stay as they are.

examples.name: Confirm a commodity row with a corrected price
examples.summary: `rowIndex` counts from 0 in the terminal listing. Send `reviewRevision` from the queue item: a stale revision (the capture was reprocessed) is rejected. `values` holds only what you corrected; prices are whole aUEC per SCU.

examples.name: Approve this on the PC
examples.summary: `code` is shown to the user, who runs `ce-companion approve <code>`. `connection` identifies this socket; `expiresInS` is how long the code is valid (120).

examples.name: The connection needs a higher scope
examples.summary: `for` is the message type that was refused and `scope` what it needs.

examples.name: The connection holds admin for ten minutes
Background work paused while the game is busy
examples.summary: `waiting` is the number of queued jobs; `until` an ISO time when the hold ends, when known.

examples.summary: `handleKey` is the lowercase handle, the key every contact table uses.

examples.name: Org sync set up and healthy
examples.summary: `pending` are outbox entries not yet sent, `rejected` those the Hub refused. `lastPullAt` and `lastPushAt` are ISO times. `role` is the Hub's view of you. `sharing` shows the four switches.
